speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are presenting with shortness of breath, increased abdominal girth, and a large ovarian mass; please allow me to ask a few questions to better understand your condition. Have you experienced any pain in your abdomen or pelvic region, and have you noticed any changes in your urinary or bowel habits?

speaker: Patient
text: 40-year-old nulliparous woman. The patient reports experiencing shortness of breath and noticeable increase in abdominal size over the past month. She denies any significant medical history, previous surgeries, or use of medications.

speaker: Doctor
text: Based on your age and the presence of a large ovarian mass causing shortness of breath and abdominal distension, I need to determine if this mass is solid or cystic and if it has ruptured. REQUEST TEST: Transabdominal Ultrasound. Additionally, do you experience any sudden, sharp pain or any bleeding between menstrual periods?

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Transabdominal Ultrasound Findings: Large mass in the right ovary, significant ascites present.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Ovarian Cancer. The combination of a large right ovarian mass and significant ascites in a 40-year-old woman is highly suggestive of malignancy. REQUEST IMAGES: CT Abdomen and Pelvis to evaluate for metastasis and staging.
